answer: Lotus is a per-epoch random probe: each epoch a VRF randomness signal selects which agents must solve a fresh micro-task in minutes, routed through Tundra, an edge-relay layer stamping every submission with verified hardware-attested compute. Cached answers never transfer because the probe changes each draw and the signal is public, so selection cannot be rigged. An attacker running N puppet addresses pays N probe fees and N attestations, and each failed draw slashes a bond - costs never amortize across the fleet, while honest users solve one probe per epoch.
